name.text: Measures of Location and Dispersion Applications-q3

questiontext.text:
Which one of the following is not a characteristic of an ideal measure of central tendency?

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]][[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked solution

[[ if test="member(1, ta_index)" ]]

They are not affected by extreme values:

This is not a characteristic of an ideal measure of central tendency. In fact, ideal measures should take into account the distribution of data, including extreme values. For example, the mean is influenced by extreme values, which can lead to skewed results. The median, on the other hand, is less affected by extreme values and is often preferred when dealing with skewed data.

[[/ if ]] [[ if test="member(2, ta_index)" ]]

They are affected by sampling fluctuations:

This is not an ideal characteristic for a measure of central tendency. Ideally, a measure of central tendency should be stable and not heavily influenced by random sampling fluctuations. The mean is affected by sampling fluctuations, whereas the median is more robust in this regard.

[[/ if ]] [[ if test="member(3, ta_index)" ]]

They are difficult to calculate:

An ideal measure of central tendency should not be difficult to calculate. Ease of calculation is generally a desirable trait. Measures like the mean and median are relatively easy to calculate, whereas more complex measures may be less practical.

[[/ if ]]
